Pricing & Discount Strategy Analysis

This is the highest-priority section for management: do deeper discounts produce higher ratings or just more reviews? The data below quantifies this relationship precisely.

Correlation Matrix

Key Correlation Findings

The correlation between discount percentage and customer rating is weak and negative (r = -0.156). The Spearman rank correlation is -0.146 (p = 0.0000), confirming this relationship is not meaningfully positive.
The correlation between discount percentage and review volume is negligible and positive (r = 0.011). Spearman rank correlation: -0.098 (p = 0.0002). Discounts show slightly more influence on review volume than on ratings, but the effect is still weak.

Discount Percentage vs. Customer Rating

The scatter plot reveals a wide dispersion with no strong upward trend. Products with low discounts are just as likely to have high ratings as deeply discounted products.

Product Price vs. Rating

Critical Finding: Deeper discounts do not correlate with higher customer ratings (r = -0.156). The relationship is near zero to slightly negative. Discounting is not a lever for improving customer satisfaction — it primarily influences volume, and even that effect is weak (r = 0.011).
Price segment insight: Lower-priced segments (<₹500) tend to carry the highest discounts but not the highest ratings, while premium segments (>₹10K) maintain strong ratings with comparatively moderate discounting — suggesting quality perception in premium categories is not discount-driven.

Common Traits of High-Engagement Products

  • Accessories dominate: The majority of top-engaged products are cables, chargers, and low-cost accessories — high-volume, low-consideration purchases.
  • Low to mid price range: Most are priced below ₹1,000 (actual price), making them impulse-friendly purchases with mass-market appeal.
  • Discount depth varies: Discounts range from 19% to 78%, reinforcing that discount depth alone doesn't drive engagement.
  • Ratings are strong but not perfect: Average rating among the top 10 engaged products is 4.22, indicating high engagement doesn't always mean perfect satisfaction.

Strategic Recommendations

Every recommendation below is grounded in the data analyzed in this report. Where a specific metric supports the recommendation, it is cited.

1. Reallocate Discount Spend from Low-Impact to Quality Investment

The correlation between discount depth and customer rating is effectively zero r = -0.156. Margins are being sacrificed without measurable gains in customer satisfaction. Redirect a portion of discount budgets toward product quality improvement, packaging, and post-sale support — the factors that actually drive the positive themes ("quality," "value for money") seen in reviews.

2. Audit and Rationalize the Car&Motorbike Category

Car&Motorbike has the lowest average rating at 3.80 across 1 products. Negative review themes center on "stopped working" and "poor quality." Conduct a product-level audit: identify sub-₹500 items dragging ratings down, remove chronic underperformers, and raise quality gates for new listings in this category.

3. Leverage the OfficeProducts Category as a Satisfaction Model

OfficeProducts leads with a 4.31 average rating. Analyze what product attributes, price points, and vendor practices make this category successful, and apply those learnings to underperforming categories. Consider expanding assortment in this category where demand is proven.

4. Calibrate Discounts by Price Segment, Not One-Size-Fits-All

Lower price segments (<₹500) carry the heaviest discounts avg 40.4% but don't achieve the highest ratings. Premium segments maintain strong ratings with moderate discounting. Adopt a tiered discount strategy: modest discounts (10-25%) for premium products where quality perception matters, and selective deeper discounts only for high-volume accessories where conversion, not satisfaction, is the goal.

5. Address Durability Concerns Highlighted in Negative Reviews

"Stopped working," "waste," and "defective" are among the top negative themes across categories, with 4,017 negative mentions catalog-wide. Invest in supplier quality requirements, warranty communication, and return process improvements. Products that fail early generate outsized negative sentiment that drags category-level ratings and erodes trust.
